challenges.name: server-client-components-quiz
challenges.title: Where does the boundary run?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the course page: the client component that pulled the page into the bundle, and an error from passing a prop across the boundary.

questions.explanation: False. "use client" marks a boundary in the module graph: the file that has it and every module it imports become client code. CourseBody imports Reviews, so Reviews is bundled for the browser even though its own file has no directive (the same happens to Syllabus and to ProgressChart with its chart library). A component without a directive is a server component only when it is imported from server code. The misconception is that the directive is a per-file label; it is an entry point, and everything behind it follows. The fix is to keep CourseBody small (only the toggle) and let the server page render Reviews, passing it in as children if it must appear inside a client component.

True. Props that go from a server component to a client component are serialized by React and sent with the page; a string serializes, an ordinary function does not, because its code and closure live on the server. When the click handling lives inside EnrollButton, the function is created in the browser and never crosses the boundary. A Server Function (marked "use server") is the exception: it crosses as a reference the client can call. The misconception is that a prop is just a JavaScript value passed in memory; across this boundary it is data on the wire, so it must be data (strings, numbers, plain objects, arrays, Dates, JSX) and not behaviour.

challenges.name: plan-client-boundaries
challenges.title: Push "use client" down to the leaves
challenges.description: On the CodeDev course page someone put "use client" at the top of the page, and the chart library and the whole page became client code. Write planBoundaries(root) for a component tree whose nodes are { name, uses?, ownKb?, libKb?, props?, children? }: uses lists features from "state", "effect", "eventHandler", "browserApi", "secret", "database"; ownKb is the component's own gzipped size and libKb a heavy library it imports; props maps each prop its parent passes to a kind; children are the components it imports and renders. Walk the tree depth-first (a parent before its children, children in the given order) and return { components, useClient, badProps, conflicts, clientKb }. components: one { name, runsOn } per component; runsOn is "client" when the component uses state, effect, eventHandler or browserApi, or when its parent runs on the client (everything a client component imports is client code), otherwise "server". useClient: the components whose file needs "use client": client components whose parent runs on the server, and the root if it runs on the client; nothing below a boundary gets it. badProps: for each "use client" component except the root, every prop its server parent passes that cannot cross the boundary, as "<Component>.<prop> (<kind>)" in prop order. Kinds that can cross: "string", "number", "boolean", "null", "array", "plainObject", "date" (React 19 serializes Date), "jsx" and "serverAction"; "function", "classInstance" and any other kind cannot. Props between two client components are never reported. conflicts: client components that use "secret" or "database". clientKb: the sum of ownKb + libKb over all client components, rounded to 1 decimal. Invalid input: a missing uses, props or children means empty; an ownKb or libKb that is missing or not a finite number >= 0 counts as 0; unknown features are ignored. The test runner reads the root as JSON and prints the plan.
hints: What does a component need to know about its parent to decide where it runs, whether it needs its own "use client" line and whether its props cross the network?

A recursive visit(node, parentRunsOn) that receives the parent's decision is enough: the root has no parent (neither server nor client), a client parent forces client, and only the step from a server parent to a client child is a boundary. Check props and add the directive at that step only. Sum the sizes as you go and round once at the end.

A similar tree that is not in the tests: QuizPage (database) renders Timer (effect, props { endsAt: date, onEnd: function }) and Question (no features); Timer renders Clock (no features, props { onTick: function }). Timer is a boundary under a server parent: it gets "use client", endsAt crosses, onEnd is reported as "Timer.onEnd (function)". Clock runs on the client because Timer imports it, needs no directive, and its onTick is not checked. Question stays on the server and adds nothing to the client size.

tests.name: The fixed course page: only the toggle, the enroll button and the chart are client code
The incident: state in the page component pulls the whole page and the chart library to the client
Functions and class instances cannot cross; a Date, JSX and a server action can
Below a boundary: no use client, no prop check, every import is client code
Conflicts: server-only code that ends up on the client, at a boundary and below one
A client root gets use client; its props and those of the components below it are not checked
Invalid input: missing fields, negative or text sizes, unknown features and prop kinds
